A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EditReward and retain matching methods, experiments, and appendices. All 24 pages of v1 and 32 pages of v2 were readable, with figures and equations visually checked.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model evaluations, Step1X-Edit fine-tuning results, architectural ablations, and positional-bias analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds annotation-agreement measurements, filtering-size experiments, an out-of-distribution evaluation, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The VLM backbones, separate Gaussian reward heads, uncertainty-aware ranking loss, score aggregation, and tie-disentanglement procedure remain unchanged. The additional filtering sizes test the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Section 4.5 adds an Open Images-sourced out-of-distribution evaluation covering text-in-image editing and style transfer. This extends the evaluated source distribution; training sources and the original benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding reward-model and GEdit-Bench comparisons retain their baseline sets. The new OOD evaluation reuses GPT-4o, while the additional Top-K rows are configurations of the existing filtering method.

E3.justification: v2 adds fine-tuning on Top-10K and Top-30K subsets alongside the existing Top-20K setting. The new OOD evaluation uses 253 text pairs and 185 style pairs with expert annotations and accuracy reporting. Existing benchmark metrics and reward-model training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis through filtering-size sensitivity, the Open Images distribution-shift test, and Appendices A.10-A.13. New examples examine annotations, retained versus rejected data, downstream editing differences, and brightness/background-preservation failures. Earlier architectural, tie-disentanglement, and positional-bias analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 describes maintaining annotation agreement without quantifying it. v2 newly reports Fleiss' kappa and Krippendorff's alpha for both scoring dimensions and dataset groups, with the same measurements displayed in Tables 2 and 9. No repeated-training-run or confidence-interval reporting is added.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are retained, but substantial new evidence is reported. Table 4 adds English overall scores of 6.938 and 6.962 for Top-10K and Top-30K, alongside the unchanged Top-20K score of 7.086. Table 5 adds OOD overall accuracy of 46.80 for EditReward versus 41.69 for GPT-4o. Agreement statistics and qualitative filtering/failure findings are also new.

T1.justification: Equations 1-6 retain the same reward definitions, Gaussian assumptions, aggregation rules, losses, and tie decomposition. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The dataset, reward model, benchmark, and downstream data-curation contributions remain unchanged. v2 removes the abstract's and conclusion's statements about potential reinforcement-learning post-training and test-time scaling, modestly narrowing the claimed application scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of lower visual-quality agreement, the quality-versus-volume tradeoff in filtering, and OOD applicability. Appendix A.13 newly identifies excessive-brightness preferences and insufficient penalties for background changes, including a proposed connection to VLM pretraining. These substantially expand the account of mechanisms and limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds scoring-time figures, explicit benchmark non-overlap confirmation, filtering disclosures, and a CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0 release statement. Section 4.1 changes A100 to A800, matching the earlier reproducibility statement. Some unchanged hyperparameters move into the main text, but Appendix A.4's AdamW coefficients, weight decay, and software versions are removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Fleiss, Krippendorff, and ImagenWorld by Sani et al. The existing related-work discussion and positioning against prior editing evaluators remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local revisions shorten the abstract and conclusion, expand the filtering and ethics discussions, update publication headers, and add an OOD subsection and four appendix subsections. There is no extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven multipanel figures covering dataset examples, filtering, downstream comparisons, and failures. It also adds agreement and OOD tables and expands the downstream results table with subset-size rows. Original Figures 1-5 are retained, with several displays relocated; agreement results are displayed twice.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's unquantified annotation-quality claims and single curated-subset size, v2 supplies agreement measurements, filtering-size sensitivity, and an additional OOD test. Failure analysis also improves transparency about applicability. These targeted gains outweigh the loss of optimizer and software details from Appendix A.4, but the reproducibility regression limits the overall improvement.
